title_en: Wang Jun v. Li Rui — dispute over mortgage contract
ruling_gist_en: If a mortgagee fails to exercise the mortgage right within the statute of limitations period for the principal claim, the mortgage right is extinguished, rather than the loss of the right to prevail. After the mortgage right is extinguished, if the mortgagor requests the cancellation of the mortgage registration, the people's court shall support such request.

full_text_en:
Wang Jun v. Li Rui — dispute over mortgage contract

Ruling Summary

Where the mortgagee fails to exercise the mortgage right during the limitation period for the principal creditor's right, the mortgage right is extinguished, rather than merely losing the right to win the lawsuit. After the mortgage right is extinguished, if the mortgagor requests the discharge of the mortgage registration, the people's court shall support such request.

Plaintiff: Wang Jun, female, 69 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Tongzhou District, Beijing.

Defendant: Li Rui, male, 35 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province.

The plaintiff, Wang Jun, instituted an action in the Tongzhou District People's Court of Beijing against the defendant, Li Rui, on a dispute over a mortgage contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations:

On August 12, 2009, Wang Jun and the defendant Li Rui entered into a real property mortgage contract and a loan contract, agreeing to use the property located at A, Tongzhou District, Beijing, registered under Wang Jun's name, as collateral, and completed the mortgage registration. Since the funds were actually borrowed by a third party, Lan Guangqing, from Li Rui, Wang Jun merely provided the title deed at Lan Guangqing's request. All repayments were to be made by Lan Guangqing personally, and had nothing to do with Wang Jun. Wang Jun was unaware of how Li Rui negotiated with Lan Guangqing. Wang Jun did not receive the loan of RMB 500,000 from Li Rui. Since the actual borrower was Lan Guangqing, and Li Rui failed to exercise the mortgage right within the limitation period for the principal creditor's right, the mortgage right should not be protected. Wang Jun now files this lawsuit, requesting the court to order: Li Rui to assist Wang Jun in completing the procedures for discharging the mortgage registration on the property at A, Tongzhou District, Beijing.

Defendant's Defense:

The defendant disagrees with the plaintiff Wang Jun's claims. On August 11, 2009, the third party Lan Guangqing approached Li Rui, stating that Wang Jun had previously borrowed money from Jiang Su and mortgaged her own property as collateral. Upon maturity of that loan, Wang Jun needed to borrow money to repay the debt. Therefore, Wang Jun borrowed RMB 500,000 from Li Rui. Both parties signed a loan agreement stipulating a monthly interest of RMB 15,000. After receiving the loan of RMB 500,000 from Li Rui, Wang Jun issued a receipt to Li Rui. Both parties agreed to mortgage the property A, Tongzhou District, Beijing, registered under Wang Jun's name, and completed the mortgage registration. A loan contract relationship and a mortgage contract relationship were established between the parties, with Li Rui being the mortgagee. After the loan, Lan Guangqing made repayments to Li Rui via bank transfer, but Li Rui also continuously called Wang Jun to demand repayment. In 2014, after losing contact with Lan Guangqing, Li Rui found Wang Jun to demand repayment, and Wang Jun herself agreed to repay. On August 3, 2015, Wang Jun repaid RMB 7,000 to Li Rui; therefore, the creditor's right in question had not exceeded the statute of limitations.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Tongzhou District People's Court of Beijing):

On August 11, 2009, Wang Jun (Party A) and Li Rui (Party B) signed an agreement stipulating:
"I. Party A borrows RMB 500,000 from Party B, with a term from August 11, 2009 to September 10, 2009. The full amount shall be repaid in one lump sum upon maturity.
II. If Party A fails to repay the entire debt upon maturity, from the maturity date until the date Party A actually repays all debts to Party B, Party A shall pay Party B overdue interest at a daily rate of 3‰ of the loan amount.
III. To secure Party B's rights and interests, Party A mortgages the property located at A, Tongzhou District, Beijing, to Party B. Meanwhile, Party A delivers to Party B for safekeeping the title deed, house purchase contract, purchase invoice, and the homeowner's ID card and other documents.
IV. If Party A fails to repay the entire debt upon maturity, in addition to paying the overdue interest as stipulated in Article II, Party A shall assist Party B in disposing of the collateral. The proceeds from the disposal shall be used to repay Party B's debt, with any shortfall to be repaid by Party A. Expenses incurred from the disposal of the collateral shall be borne by Party A.
...
VI. This agreement is made in duplicate, held by each party, and has equal legal effect. It is effective from the date of signature by both parties until the date Party A repays all debts to Party B. Matters not covered herein, if not resolved through negotiation, shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Tongzhou District People's Court of Beijing."
Wang Jun signed and confirmed as Party A; Li Rui signed and confirmed as Party B.
On the same day, RMB 497,200 was transferred from Li Rui's bank card account to another account. Wang Jun issued a receipt to Li Rui stating: "Received cash of RMB 500,000 from Li Rui in full."
On August 12, 2009, Wang Jun and Li Rui completed the mortgage registration procedures for the subject property at the Beijing Tongzhou District Construction Committee. On September 2, 2009, Li Rui was registered as the other-rights holder of the above property and obtained the other-rights certificate for Property A, which recorded Wang Jun as the property owner and the amount of the creditor's right as RMB 500,000.

During the trial, the defendant Li Rui stated that in August 2009, Lan Guangqing approached him, stating that the plaintiff Wang Jun had borrowed RMB 500,000 from Jiang Su, secured by two properties registered under Wang Jun's name. The repayment deadline was approaching, and Wang Jun was unable to repay, so she wanted to borrow from Li Rui to repay the debt, agreeing to use Wang Jun's property as collateral. Li Rui, considering Wang Jun's situation, agreed to Wang Jun's request. At that time, Li Rui transferred RMB 497,200 to an account designated by Wang Jun and gave Wang Jun RMB 2,800 in cash. After the transfer, at the real estate management authority, Wang Jun and Li Rui signed the above agreement, and Wang Jun issued a receipt to Li Rui. Since the borrowed funds were used to repay Jiang Su's loan, after repayment, Jiang Su agreed to cancel the mortgage registration. Wang Jun and Li Rui completed the mortgage registration procedures for the subject property. On September 2, 2009, Li Rui was registered as the other-rights holder and obtained the other-rights certificate. At the time of borrowing, Wang Jun stated that she would pay monthly interest but did not specify when she would repay the principal. Subsequently, Li Rui called Wang Jun to demand repayment, and Wang Jun always said to contact Lan Guangqing to have him repay. At that time, the agreed monthly interest was RMB 15,000. After the loan, Lan Guangqing made repayments to Li Rui, but not on schedule. Until September 2014, Li Rui could not contact Lan Guangqing and directly approached Wang Jun to demand repayment. Wang Jun agreed to repay at that time. In June 2015, Li Rui approached Wang Jun to negotiate repayment. Wang Jun took Li Rui to meet Li Lianxia, who agreed to repay RMB 200,000 to Li Rui and discharge the mortgage registration. On August 3, 2015, Wang Jun repaid RMB 7,000 to Li Rui.

The plaintiff Wang Jun did not acknowledge the borrowing process as stated by the defendant Li Rui. Wang Jun stated that Li Lianxia was her student, and Lan Guangqing was Li Lianxia's friend. At that time, Li Lianxia and Lan Guangqing approached Wang Jun together. Lan Guangqing stated that he needed to borrow from a guarantee company to build greenhouses in Taihu, but because he did not have a property with full title under his own name as collateral, he wanted to borrow Wang Jun's title deed as collateral. Lan Guangqing borrowed from Jiang Su and completed the mortgage registration. Later, because Lan Guangqing had no money to repay Jiang Su and needed to borrow again, he told Wang Jun that he would borrow again from Li Rui and complete the property mortgage procedures. At that time, Lan Guangqing told Wang Jun that the loan had nothing to do with Wang Jun, she did not need to repay, and only needed to provide the title deed. After the loan, Li Rui never contacted Wang Jun. It was not until around April 2015 that Li Rui found Wang Jun to ask for Lan Guangqing's contact information, but did not demand repayment from Wang Jun. It was not until September 2015 that Li Rui demanded Wang Jun to repay the loan. Wang Jun clearly stated that the loan had nothing to do with her and refused to repay. She claimed never to have repaid RMB 7,000 to Li Rui.

Upon inquiry by the court, the defendant Li Rui stated that there were other loan transactions between him and Lan Guangqing. Lan Guangqing transferred money to Li Rui, but Lan Guangqing never clearly indicated that the repayments were for the plaintiff Wang Jun's loan. Therefore, Li Rui could not specify whether Lan Guangqing's repayments were for Wang Jun's loan.

Separately, the property owner of property A, Tongzhou District, Beijing, was the plaintiff Wang Jun. On May 14, 2009, Wang Jun and a third party, Jiang Su, signed a mortgage contract, whereby Wang Jun mortgaged the above property to Jiang Su. The mortgage registration was completed on May 27, 2009, for a total loan of RMB 350,000. On August 11, 2009, Wang Jun and Jiang Su submitted a cancellation agreement to the Beijing Tongzhou District Construction Committee, stating that the RMB 350,000 loan had been fully repaid on August 11, 2009, and requesting cancellation of the mortgage registration. On the same day, the Beijing Tongzhou District Construction Committee cancelled that mortgage registration.

The above facts are confirmed by the agreement, receipt, title deed, inquiry results from the Beijing Tongzhou District Real Estate Registration Affairs Center, the other-rights certificate, property registration archival materials, bank transaction details, and statements of the parties.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Tongzhou District People's Court of Beijing):

The parties have the burden to provide evidence to prove the facts on which their claims are based or to rebut the facts on which the opposing party's claims are based. If there is no evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove the factual assertions of a party, that party, who bears the burden of proof, shall bear the adverse consequences. In this case, the plaintiff Wang Jun and the defendant Li Rui signed the loan agreement and the property mortgage guarantee agreement, and Wang Jun issued a receipt to Li Rui. These represented the true intentions of both parties. As the borrower, Wang Jun should repay the loan according to the agreement. The loan agreement stipulated that the repayment date was September 10, 2009. Therefore, the limitation period for Li Rui to seek protection of his civil rights should be from September 11, 2009 to September 10, 2011. Li Rui, as the mortgagee, should exercise the mortgage right within the limitation period for the principal creditor's right.

During the trial, the defendant Li Rui claimed that after the loan, Lan Guangqing repaid Li Rui by transfer. However, because there were other loan transactions between Li Rui and Lan Guangqing, and Lan Guangqing did not clearly state whether the repayments were for the loan of the plaintiff Wang Jun, and Li Rui could not provide evidence to prove that Lan Guangqing explicitly expressed the intention to repay on behalf of Wang Jun, the adverse consequences shall be borne by Li Rui. Therefore, the repayments by Lan Guangqing as stated by Li Rui cannot constitute grounds for interruption of the statute of limitations for the creditor's right. Considering the evidence submitted by both parties, Li Rui did not submit relevant evidence to prove that he asserted his rights against Wang Jun within the above period, nor did he submit evidence to prove that Wang Jun repaid the loan to Li Rui. Therefore, the above creditor's right has exceeded the statute of limitations. Since Li Rui, as the mortgagee, did not exercise the mortgage right within the limitation period for the principal creditor's right, the mortgage right has been extinguished. Wang Jun now requests that Li Rui assist in completing the procedures for cancelling the mortgage registration on the property at A, Tongzhou District, Beijing. The court supports this claim. Since Wang Jun and Li Rui signed the loan agreement and the property mortgage guarantee agreement, even if the borrower and the actual user of the funds are inconsistent, this does not affect the privity and validity of the loan contract. Therefore, whether the payee's account name is Wang Jun does not affect the determination of this case. The court does not accept Wang Jun's argument that she was not the actual borrower. Li Rui argued that after the loan, he continuously demanded repayment from Wang Jun, and that on August 3, 2015, Wang Jun repaid RMB 7,000 to Li Rui. Because Li Rui did not submit relevant evidence to prove this, the court does not accept the above defense.

In conclusion, in accordance with Article 135 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 202 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Tongzhou District People's Court of Beijing rendered the following judgment on June 13, 2016:

The plaintiff Wang Jun and the defendant Li Rui shall, within seven days from the effective date of this judgment, complete the procedures for cancelling the mortgage registration on the property at A, Tongzhou District, Beijing, registered under the name of the plaintiff Wang Jun.

Li Rui disagreed with the judgment of first instance and appealed to the Beijing Third Intermediate People's Court, stating: The mortgage loan contract between the appellee Wang Jun and Li Rui genuinely exists, and Wang Jun has not repaid the debt in full. I do not agree to discharge the mortgage. During the limitation period, I repeatedly demanded repayment, and Wang Jun once repaid RMB 7,000. Therefore, there is no issue of exceeding the statute of limitations. Accordingly, Li Rui requested the court of second instance to revoke the original judgment and dismiss Wang Jun's claims.

The appellee Wang Jun argued in defense: The loan was borrowed by Lan Guangqing from the appellant Li Rui. I was merely a guarantor, using my title deed as collateral. I did not borrow money from Li Rui; the repayment should be made by Lan Guangqing. Moreover, even if Li Rui asserted his creditor's right against me, it has exceeded the statute of limitations. Li Rui has no evidence to prove that I repaid money, which would cause the statute of limitations to be interrupted. In conclusion, Wang Jun requested that the judgment of first instance be affirmed.

Upon retrial, the Beijing Third Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Opinion of the Court at Second Instance (Beijing Third Intermediate People's Court):

The focus of the dispute in this case centers on three issues: First, whether a loan legal relationship existed between the appellee Wang Jun and the appellant Li Rui; second, if a loan legal relationship was established, whether the principal creditor's right held by Li Rui had exceeded the statute of limitations; third, if the principal creditor's right had exceeded the statute of limitations, whether the mortgage right established to secure the principal creditor's right is extinguished, i.e., whether the mortgagor Wang Jun's request to discharge the mortgage registration should be supported.

Regarding the first issue, the court holds that a loan legal relationship existed between the appellee Wang Jun and the appellant Li Rui. The reasons are as follows: First, the agreement dated August 11, 2009, containing the loan terms, indicated that the parties were Wang Jun and Li Rui. On the same day, Wang Jun issued a receipt for RMB 500,000 to Li Rui, which also stated the payee as Wang Jun. Second, on August 12, 2009, Wang Jun, based on the above loan agreement, applied to the relevant authority for mortgage registration using her own property, clearly designating Li Rui, the lender of the said funds, as the mortgagee. Third, the lender Li Rui clearly stated during the trial that Wang Jun was the borrower. Although Wang Jun claimed that the funds involved in this case were not borrowed by her but were used as collateral on her property for the third party Lan Guangqing, Wang Jun did not provide counter-evidence and, during the court trial, explicitly stated that she accepted the legal relationship determined by the court of first instance. Therefore, considering the form of the legal relationship and the party's admission, it should be determined that the loan legal relationship existed between Wang Jun and Li Rui.

Regarding the second issue, assuming the loan legal relationship is established, the court holds that the appellant Li Rui's creditor's right has exceeded the statute of limitations. The reasons are as follows: First, according to the agreement signed by both parties, the appellee Wang Jun should have repaid the loan on September 11, 2009. If Wang Jun failed to repay on time, Li Rui's creditor's right was infringed upon from that date. Pursuant to Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Li Rui should have asserted his creditor's right against Wang Jun before September 10, 2011; otherwise, the people's court would not protect it. Second, Li Rui admitted that he did not directly approach Wang Jun to demand repayment before 2014, explaining that before 2014, he communicated with Wang Jun by phone, and the third party Lan Guangqing repaid on behalf of Wang Jun. However, Li Rui also stated that besides the loan in dispute, there were other creditor-debt relationships between him and Lan Guangqing. Li Rui was unclear as to which debt the repayments made by Lan Guangqing corresponded to. Moreover, setting aside the nature of Lan Guangqing's repayments, Li Rui did not submit any evidence to support the phone communication or the fact that Lan Guangqing had repaid him. Third, Li Rui argued that Wang Jun had repaid RMB 5,000 to him in August 2015. To support this, Li Rui submitted only an audio recording. However, since Wang Jun denied this and the content of the recording lacked clear direction, it is difficult for the court to find that there was a reason to bar the statute of limitations. Therefore, based on the above analysis, it should be determined that Li Rui did not actively assert his creditor's right against Wang Jun before the expiration of the statute of limitations, i.e., before September 10, 2011, and there was no other ground to prevent the running of the statute of limitations. Consequently, Li Rui has lost the right to seek court protection for the above creditor's right.

Regarding the third issue, under the premise that the principal creditor's right has exceeded the statute of limitations, the court holds that the appellant Li Rui's mortgage right has been extinguished, and the mortgagor Wang Jun's request to discharge the mortgage registration should be supported. However, it is necessary to specifically point out that since the essence of this issue involves the interpretation of Article 202 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Property Law) and is directly related to the parties' claims and defenses, the court, based on legal principles and statutory norms, sets forth the reasons for the above determination as follows:

Article 202 of the Property Law provides: "The mortgagee shall exercise the mortgage right within the limitation period for the principal creditor's right; if not exercised, the people's court shall not protect it." The clarification of the meaning of "shall not protect" in this provision depends on the analysis of the nature of the statute of limitations and the mortgage right.

First, as to the statute of limitations, its regulatory target is the situation where the obligee neglects to exercise the right continuously until a statutory period has elapsed. Its purpose is to cause the obligee whose claim has become time-barred to bear disadvantages, thereby urging him to exercise his right in a timely manner. According to general civil law theory, its scope of application is limited to the right to claim in personam. As for the mortgage right, it is a right in rem (a right of control), not within the scope of the right to claim, nor within the scope of the right to claim in personam. Including the mortgage right within the scope of the statute of limitations would undoubtedly contradict civil law principles.

Second, as to the mortgage right, its purpose is to secure the performance of the debt and ensure that the mortgagee enjoys the right to be paid in priority from the value of the mortgaged property. To achieve this purpose, the mortgage right necessarily imposes limitations on the powers of the property itself, affecting its use and transfer. Therefore, if the period for the mortgagee to exercise the mortgage right is not limited, the ownership of the mortgaged property will remain in an unstable state for a long time, which is not conducive to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, nor to the use and circulation of property. Furthermore, if the mortgagee is allowed to exercise the mortgage right at any time, it would mean that even after the principal creditor's right has become time-barred and the debtor has thus obtained the right of defense, the creditor could still obtain benefits from the mortgagor, thereby placing the mortgagor and the debtor's rights of recourse and defense in difficulty. In other words, it would also mean that the mortgagor would long remain in a disadvantageous state with uncertain obligations. If so, this would be too harsh and unfair to the mortgagor.

Third, from the perspective of the classification of rights, when several rights coexist, according to the interdependence of rights, there are principal rights and accessory rights. A right that can exist independently without relying on other rights is a principal right; a right that must be attached to another right and cannot exist independently is an accessory right. For example, when a right to claim in personam and a mortgage right securing the performance of the obligation coexist, the right to claim in personam is the principal right, and the mortgage right is the accessory right. In a situation where the principal right has lost the protection of state coercive power, the mortgage right burdening the mortgaged property should also be extinguished to better utilize the property's utility, which is consistent with the internal logic of the security interest system under the Property Law. Therefore, one of the important purposes of Article 202 of the Property Law in establishing the period for exercising the mortgage right is to encourage the mortgagee to actively exercise the mortgage right, promptly settle the creditor-debt relationship, and maintain the stability of social and economic order. Based on the above analysis, it should be determined that if, after the law has set a period for exercise, the mortgagee remains inactive for a long time, there is no need for the law to provide special protection; the mortgage right should be extinguished. Applying this to the present case, since the appellant Li Rui did not assert his mortgage right against the appellee Wang Jun during the limitation period for the principal creditor's right, the people's court will not protect Li Rui's mortgage right; such mortgage right is extinguished. Wang Jun's request to discharge the mortgage registration should be supported.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Beijing Third Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 25, 2016:

Appeal dismissed. Original judgment affirmed.

This judgment is final.
